newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tax probe continues at Germany's WestLB.
newsitem.headline: Tax probe continues at Germany's WestLB.

text.p: German tax authorities investigating suspected tax evasion have not yet concluded searches at branches of Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale, a prosecutor said on Friday.
Jochen Ruhland, prosecutor in the town of Duesseldorf, said that the searches at branches of the bank and at some savings banks would continue into next week.

The prosecutor's office said on Tuesday that investigators from the finance office and the prosecutor's office were investigating suspicions that employees from the institutions may have helped bank customers evade paying taxes.
There were also suspicions of illegal transfers of funds to Luxembourg and, in certain cases, to Switzerland. Indications of possible tax irregularities emerged during an audit.
Ruhland said around 600 officials had been involved so far in the search for evidence.
WestLB issued a statement earlier this week confirming that it was under investigation and said it would provide as much assistance to officials as possible without breaching bank secrecy laws.

The investigation is the latest in a string of incidents where authorities have swooped down on Germany's largest banks over the past two years searching offices and seizing documents in a crackdown on alleged bank abetment to tax evasion.
The probes follow the exodus of billions of marks to Luxembourg and other tax havens after Germany slapped a 30 percent withholding tax on interest income in 1994.
Moving funds abroad to avoid that tax is not in itself illegal, but failing to report interest income to fiscal authorities in Germany is in breach of the law.
